title: Cipher and Parish
premise: Quentin Pemberton, the coroner of the fading parish town of Hollowmere, is hired by a nervous stranger who pays triple rate to prove that a murder has not yet happened — a murder he insists will occur on the night of the town's founding festival. As Quentin investigates, she discovers the plot threads back to an unsolved death thirty years ago, one her own late father helped bury, literally and otherwise. The would-be victim turns out to be the man everyone in town trusts most, and the conspiracy of silence stretches through half the families on the parish roll. In the end Quentin must choose between the law's tidy verdict and a justice the town can actually live with, exposing the truth at the cost of her father's name — and finding, among the people who finally stop lying to her, the family she never had.
about_author: F. M. Marchetti spent a decade as a records clerk in rural county offices, where the ledgers taught her more about human nature than any confession ever did. She writes mysteries from a converted chapel, insisting that every good crime story is really a story about what a community agrees not to see.

chapters.title: The Advance Payment
chapters.summary: POV: Quentin. A stranger named Elias Wren arrives at the coroner's office with cash and an impossible request: prove a murder hasn't happened yet. He names no victim, only a date — the founding festival, three weeks out. The beat is unease; Quentin's professional pride is hooked by a puzzle that shouldn't exist.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: POV: Quentin. Walking the cemetery to clear her head, Quentin catalogs the parish dead and realizes Wren's date coincides with the thirtieth anniversary of Thomas Aldery's drowning — ruled accidental by her father's own hand. The emotional beat is inherited doubt: for the first time she questions the verdicts she grew up trusting.

chapters.title: The Festival Committee
chapters.summary: POV: Quentin. At the planning meeting, Quentin watches the town's pillars — Mayor Odette Crane, banker Silas Vane, and beloved doctor Ambrose Hale — and notes how quickly they close ranks when she asks about old records. Beat: quiet menace beneath small-town warmth; someone is already watching her.

chapters.title: Wren's Conditions
chapters.summary: POV: Elias Wren. Through Wren's eyes we learn his terms: no police, no publicity, results by festival night. He reveals only that the intended victim is 'someone this town cannot afford to lose.' Beat: ambiguity deepens — Wren seems less like a client than a man paying to confess something.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Watermarks
chapters.summary: POV: Quentin. Digging into county archives, Quentin finds pages excised from the 1994 inquest file — cut so cleanly it took authority, not haste. Her deputy, young Tam Okafor, proves unexpectedly gifted at reconstruction. Beat: first alliance; found family begins forming around shared curiosity.

chapters.title: The Doctor's Kindness
chapters.summary: POV: Quentin. Dr. Hale offers Quentin help and warmth, patching up Tam after a fall and defending her against the mayor's warnings. Yet a detail nags: Hale was the last person to see Thomas Aldery alive. Beat: charm laced with dread; the reader suspects what Quentin refuses to.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Alibis
chapters.summary: POV: Quentin. Interviewing aging witnesses, Quentin maps a perfect lattice of alibis from the night Aldery drowned — too perfect, rehearsed across decades. Each account matches down to the weather. Beat: mounting vertigo; the whole town may be an accomplice or a hostage.

chapters.title: What My Father Signed
chapters.summary: POV: Quentin. In her late father's effects, Quentin finds his annotated copy of the inquest, with a single marginal note: 'Not the river.' Grief curdles into betrayal. Beat: personal stakes ignite — the case is now about her own bloodline's complicity.

chapters.title: A Threat Delivered Politely
chapters.summary: POV: Quentin. Mayor Crane invites Quentin to tea and gently suggests she drop the anniversary angle, invoking her office's budget dependence. That night her office window is broken — nothing stolen. Beat: fear arrives, but so does defiance; Quentin refuses to be managed.

chapters.title: Tam Follows the Money
chapters.summary: POV: Tam Okafor. Tam traces land transfers showing Aldery's riverside property passed quietly to Vane's bank weeks after his death. Someone notices him looking. Beat: the apprentice becomes a target; loyalty between mentor and deputy hardens into something familial.

chapters.title: Wren Breaks
chapters.summary: POV: Elias Wren. Cornered by Quentin, Wren admits he is Thomas Aldery's son, raised abroad, returned after finding his mother's letters. He believes the planned murder is retaliation for his digging — and that the victim is himself. Beat: pity and suspicion entwine; is Wren prey or bait?

chapters.title: The Second Body
chapters.summary: POV: Quentin. A retired constable from the 1994 case is found dead in his boathouse — staged, Quentin can tell, by someone who knows how autopsies read. Now there is a murder before the predicted one. Beat: horror and guilt; the clock Wren described is running faster than promised.

chapters.title: Hollowmere Remembers Wrong
chapters.summary: POV: Quentin. Quentin reconstructs the true sequence of Aldery's death using tide charts and the constable's hidden notebook: he was struck ashore, then moved to the water. Half the town's cherished memories are built on the cover story. Beat: righteous anger; the theme of justice outside the law sharpens.

chapters.title: Vane's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV: Quentin. Banker Vane offers Quentin money and silence, claiming he only profited from the death, never caused it — and points her toward 'the one who gave the order.' Beat: corruption admits itself; the conspiracy's architecture becomes visible, but its center stays dark.

chapters.title: The Night Watch
chapters.summary: POV: Tam. Tam and Quentin stake out the cemetery, expecting evidence tampering, and instead witness Dr. Hale laying flowers on Aldery's grave — weeping. Beat: heartbreak over certainty; the kindest man in town carries the heaviest secret, and Quentin must decide whether kindness absolves.

chapters.title: Confession at the Chapel
chapters.summary: POV: Quentin. Hale tells Quentin everything: as a young doctor he covered up Aldery's accidental killing during a drunken scuffle involving the town's founding families, trading his silence for their protection — and thirty years of being loved for it. Beat: tragic recognition; belonging bought with a lie.

chapters.title: Festival Eve
chapters.summary: POV: Quentin. Preparations glitter while Quentin pieces together the final logic: the threatened murder isn't Wren's — it's the town eliminating Hale before he can recant publicly tomorrow. She has hours, no legal standing, and allies who are barely more than strangers. Beat: breathless convergence.

chapters.title: The Founding Fire
chapters.summary: POV: Quentin. During the festival's bonfire ceremony, Quentin interrupts the ritual to expose the conspiracy before the assembled town, backed by Hale's written confession and Tam's documents. Crane moves to have her seized; the crowd wavers between its myths and its conscience. Beat: climax — truth spoken aloud at maximum cost.

chapters.title: Justice, Improvised
chapters.summary: POV: Quentin. With the sheriff compromised, the townspeople themselves detain Crane and force the reopening of both cases. Quentin chooses testimony over procedure, knowing some guilty will plead down and some innocent will suffer exposure. Beat: bittersweet triumph; law restored only because people first acted outside it.

chapters.title: Exhumation
chapters.summary: POV: Quentin. Aldery's grave is opened under new orders, and the remains confirm Quentin's reconstruction. Standing at the site, she formally amends her father's verdict in the record — grief, shame, and release braided together. Beat: catharsis; the past is re-buried honestly at last.

chapters.title: What the Town Owes
chapters.summary: POV: Tam. Through Tam's eyes, Hollowmere begins its reckoning: resignations, reparations to Aldery's family, and Wren deciding to stay rather than vanish. The town that lied to itself starts learning to tell the truth in smaller ways. Beat: hope earned, not given; found family solidifies.

chapters.title: Cipher and Parish
chapters.summary: POV: Quentin. Months later, Quentin closes a routine case in her office — now shared with Tam and visited freely by Wren — and adds a new name to her mental map of graves, this time with nothing hidden beneath it. Beat: quiet resolution; belonging, justice, and family finally share one address.
